Methods","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":91,"printedEnd":102,"pdfStart":109,"pdfEnd":120,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Neuroscientists relate brain and behavior in several ways: examining the effects of damage, stimulating brain areas, recording activity, and comparing anatomical differences with behavior."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Each method gives a different kind of evidence. Ask whether a result identifies a necessary area, an area capable of producing an effect, or only a correlation. That distinction helps when reading the research described in later chapters."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-1","text":"Four broad research approaches"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers can examine effects of damage, stimulate a brain region, record activity, or relate anatomy to behavior across people and conditions. Lesions offer clues about necessity when a function is impaired after injury, though damage can affect connected networks. Stimulation can reveal what altering a structure makes possible or more likely, but unnatural activation does not necessarily reproduce normal function. Recording methods measure what happens during a behavior, often showing correlation without proving causation."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-2","text":"What recording methods actually measure"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Different instruments provide different information. Electrical recordings can track rapid changes with high temporal precision but may provide limited localization. Methods based on blood flow or metabolism offer useful spatial patterns but are indirect measures of neural activity and usually change more slowly. Anatomical imaging shows structures; functional imaging concerns changing activity. Do not interpret a bright spot on an image as a direct photograph of a thought."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-3","text":"Strengths, limitations, and triangulation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research designs differ in spatial resolution, temporal resolution, invasiveness, and the extent to which they can support causal conclusions. A technique that locates where something happens may be poor at showing when; a technique that records rapid events may make precise location difficult. Strong inferences emerge when multiple methods point toward the same explanation. Always identify the actual comparison group and the task the participants performed."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-4","text":"How to evaluate an empirical claim"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ask five questions: What did the investigators manipulate? What did they measure? Was the result a relation or a causal test? Could the findings reflect other brain areas or wider networks? How well does the result generalize beyond the specific subjects and task? This habit will help throughout the book because virtually every later chapter relies on evidence from several methods."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h01","text":"Effects of Brain Damage"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This discovery revolutionized neurology, because it demonstrated for the first time that different brain areas have different functions.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Since then, researchers have made countless reports of behavioral impairments after brain damage.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain damage can impair the ability to recognize faces, to perceive motion, or to pay attention to the left side of the world.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although many interesting results come from people with brain damage, human studies have limitations.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Few people have damage confined to just one brain area, and each person’s pattern of brain damage is unique.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An ablation is the removal of a brain area, generally with a surgical knife.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"surface of the brain, researchers sometimes make a lesion , meaning damage, by means of a stereotaxic instrument , a device for the precise placement of electrodes in the brain (Figure 3.27).","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For comparison, the experimenter produces a sham lesion in a control group, performing all the same procedures except for passing the electrical current.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This procedure enables researchers to study behavior with a brain area active, then inactive, and then active again.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After any kind of brain damage or inactivation, the problem for psychologists is to specify the exact behavioral deficit.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h02","text":"Effects of Brain Stimulation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The old-fashioned way is to insert an electrode into an animal’s brain and deliver brief, mild currents to an area.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That method has limited value, because the electrical current stimulates many types of neurons in an area, as well as the axons passing through.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A popular approach today is optogenetics , using light to control a limited population of neurons.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One protein reacts to light by opening a sodium channel, exciting the neuron, and another reacts by opening a chloride channel, producing inhibition.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The second step was to develop viruses that insert one of these proteins into a certain type of neuron, or even to just one part","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Using these methods, an investigator can excite or inhibit a single type of neuron in a small brain area with millisecond accuracy, determining the function of cells in greater detail than ever before.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of the invasive nature of the method, it could be used in humans only when it might produce a medical benefit.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h03","text":"Recording Brain Activity"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During any behavior or experience, activity increases in some brain areas and decreases in others.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers modify the fish genetically so that proteins in the brain fluoresce when a neuron is active.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For many years, researchers relied on inserting an electrode to record activity from one neuron.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"New technologies enable researchers to use tiny electrodes that record from hundreds of neurons at once, without significantly interrupting normal function .","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Occasionally, researchers insert electrodes to record activity while a human brain is exposed preliminary to brain surgery.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The same device used for an EEG can also record brain activity in response to a stimulus, in which case we call the results evoked potentials or evoked responses .","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers using an MEG can identify the times when various brain areas respond and thereby trace a wave of brain activity from its origin to the other areas that process it .","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the most active brain areas increase their intake of glucose, tracking the glucose identifies areas of increased activity.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The computer uses this information to determine which areas have the most glucose, which are therefore the areas with greatest activity .","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For most purposes, researchers have replaced PET scans with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) , which is less expensive and less risky.","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An fMRI is a modified version based on hemoglobin (the blood protein that binds oxygen) instead of water.","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h04","text":"Correlating Brain Anatomy with Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One of the first ways ever used for studying brain function sounds easy: Find someone with unusual behavior and then look for unusual features of the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the 1800s, Franz Gall observed some people with excellent verbal memories who had protruding eyes.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"He inferred that verbal memory depended on brain areas behind the eyes that had pushed the eyes forward.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"He assumed that bulges and depressions on their skull corresponded to the brain areas below them.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If people with a particular psychological strength or weakness share some unusual feature of the brain, then we can draw inferences about that brain area.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Phrenologists’ problems were, first, that the bumps on the skull don’t correlate reliably with the anatomy of the","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"brain beneath them, and second, that the phrenologists drew conclusions based on small numbers of people and analyzed their behavior only superficially.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, to study the brain differences associated with normal behaviors, researchers would generally need large samples, probably a thousand or more, to get reliable results .","sourcePrintedPage":97,"sourcePdfPage":115,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, researchers reported correlations between the size of the amygdala and people’s political orientation or their number of Facebook friends, based on small samples.","sourcePrintedPage":97,"sourcePdfPage":115,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h05","text":"In Closing: Research Methods and Progress"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In any scientific field—indeed, any field of knowledge— progress almost always depends on improved measurement.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In astronomy, improvements in both ground-based and satellite-based astronomy have established conclusions that even science-fiction writers couldn’t have imagined.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Similarly, our understanding of the brain has advanced greatly because of the introduction of PET scans, fMRI, optogenetics, and other modern technologies.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Future progress will continue to depend on further improvements in measurement.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary, at the end of this book.","sourcePrintedPage":99,"sourcePdfPage":117,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Certain unusual aspects of brain structure were observed in the brain of Albert Einstein .","sourcePrintedPage":99,"sourcePdfPage":117,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One interpretation is that he was born with certain specialized brain features that encouraged his scientific and intellectual abilities.","sourcePrintedPage":99,"sourcePdfPage":117,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Additional patients with speech impairments also exhibited damage in and around that area, now known as Broca’s area.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"The implications are deep: If you lose part of your brain, you lose part of your mind.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"By consulting a stereotaxic atlas (map) of a species’ brain, a researcher aims an electrode at the desired position relative to landmarks on the skull.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"The researcher anesthetizes an animal, drills a small hole in the skull, inserts the electrode (insulated except at the tip), lowers it to the target, and passes an electrical current to damage that area.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), the application of magnetic stimulation to a portion of the scalp, stimulates neurons below the magnet if the stimulation is brief and mild, but with stronger stimulation it inactivates the neurons, producing a “virtual lesion” that outlasts the magnetic stimulation itself.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"If damaging a brain area makes an animal stop eating, you don’t know why.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"If brain damage impairs a behavior, stimulation should increase it.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"Development of this method required three steps, each of which would be useless without the others, and each of which seemed almost impossible.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"The first step was to discover or invent a protein that responds to light by producing an electrical current.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"Certain microbes produce such proteins, which researchers found ways to modify.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"The third step was to develop very thin optical fibers that can shine just the right amount of light onto neurons in a narrowly targeted area.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"This method demonstrated that one set of neurons responds while the fish hunts for food, another set responds while the fish swims to explore a new area, and yet another set controls transitions between hunting and exploring.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"To record brain activity in mammals, researchers use other methods.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"An electroencephalograph (EEG) records electrical activity of the brain through electrodes, ranging from just a few to more than a hundred, attached to the scalp.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"A magnetoencephalograph (MEG) is similar, but instead of measuring electrical activity, it measures the faint magnetic responses generated by brain activity.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"Positron-emission tomography (PET) provides a high-resolution image of activity in a living brain.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"PET scans use radioactive chemicals with a short half-life, made in a device called a cyclotron.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112},{"type":"bullet","text":"An fMRI while you were, for example, reading would mean nothing without a comparison to something else.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":95,"sourcePdfPage":113},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers would record your brain activity while you were reading and during a comparison task, and then compare the brain activity for the two tasks.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":95,"sourcePdfPage":113},{"type":"bullet","text":"The results provide good evidence for general trends, but in most cases, they are not reliable enough to draw conclusions about an individual person.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":95,"sourcePdfPage":113},{"type":"bullet","text":"Gall then examined the skulls of people with other talents or personalities.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"His process of relating skull anatomy to behavior is known as phrenology.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"Today, researchers can examine detailed brain anatomy in living people.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"One method is computerized axial tomography, better known as a CT or CAT areas.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":97,"sourcePdfPage":115},{"type":"bullet","text":"Weather prediction is vastly more accurate than it used to decreases.","printedPage":94,"pdfPage":112,"kind":"source_selected_detail","paragraphIndex":120026,"sourceEdition":"Kalat_14e"},{"text":"of activity, but only approximate information about location, and they are sensitive only to cells near the surface of the brain.","printedPage":95,"pdfPage":113,"kind":"source_selected_detail","paragraphIndex":120027,"sourceEdition":"Kalat_14e"},{"text":"If the dorsal striatum later becomes active while people are doing something, does that activity mean that people find the activity rewarding?","printedPage":95,"pdfPage":113,"kind":"source_selected_detail","paragraphIndex":120028,"sourceEdition":"Kalat_14e"},{"text":"The results provide good evidence for general trends, but in most cases, they are not reliable enough to draw conclusions about an individual person.","printedPage":95,"pdfPage":113,"kind":"source_selected_detail","paragraphIndex":120029,"sourceEdition":"Kalat_14e"}],"sourceBodyWords":1029,"addedWords":124,"sourceParagraphs":7},{"headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","title":"Correlating and Evolution of Behavior","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":104,"printedEnd":116,"pdfStart":122,"pdfEnd":134,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Behavior reflects interacting genetic and environmental influences. Mendelian inheritance, sex-linked and sex-limited genes, genetic change, and epigenetics describe different ways biological differences arise."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heritability describes variation within a particular population; it does not mean a behavior cannot change with experience. Evolutionary explanations address how traits may have developed, but proposed adaptive explanations require careful evidence."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-1","text":"Genes, environments, and development"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genes influence biological systems through the production and regulation of proteins. Mendelian inheritance describes how some traits are transmitted, but many behavioral characteristics involve multiple genes and environmental conditions. Sex-linked genes reside on sex chromosomes, while sex-limited effects can depend on bodily context. Mutations generate variation; changes in gene expression can also occur without changing DNA sequence. Epigenetic regulation concerns processes that influence how genes are expressed. It should not be treated as evidence that every experience rewrites DNA."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-2","text":"Understanding heritability correctly"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heritability estimates how much variation in a trait within a particular population and environment is statistically related to genetic variation. It does not tell us what fraction of one person's behavior was 'caused by genes,' nor does a high estimate make a characteristic unchangeable. When environments vary or populations differ, estimates can change. Genetic and environmental influences are not opposing percentages of a person; they interact during development."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-3","text":"Evolutionary reasoning"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evolution acts across generations when inherited variation influences survival or reproduction. A proposed evolutionary explanation of behavior must be assessed using evidence rather than assuming every trait is a perfectly optimized adaptation. Some characteristics are by-products, constraints, or consequences of changing environments. Evolutionary psychology asks how behavioral tendencies may have developed, but a plausible story is not proof. Distinguish a behavior's current function from its historical origins."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-4","text":"An exam-ready contrast"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mendelian genetics concerns patterns of inheritance; quantitative genetics often considers many genes and population variation; epigenetics concerns regulation of expression; evolutionary explanations consider changes across generations. Environmental modification can change how inherited tendencies appear. The correct study question is rarely 'nature or nurture?' It is how particular genetic, developmental, and situational influences jointly shape the outcome."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h01","text":"Mendelian Genetics"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mendel’s results demonstrated that inheritance occurs through genes , units of heredity that maintain their structural identity from one generation to another.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most genes come in pairs because they are aligned along chromosomes (strands of genes) that come in pairs.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An exception to this rule is that a male mammal has unpaired X and Y chromosomes.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Classically, a gene has been defined as part of a chromosome, which is composed of the double-stranded molecule deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) .","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes a genetic outcome depends on parts of two or more chromosomes.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It’s an amazingly simple code, considering the complexity of body structures and functions that result from it.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because each has one high taste sensitivity gene—let’s abbreviate it “T”—both parents readily taste PTC.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Therefore, a child in this family has a 25 percent chance of two T genes, a 50 percent chance of the heterozygous condition, and a 25 percent chance of being homozygous for the t gene.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, an example like this can be misleading, because it implies that a single gene produces a single outcome.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have identified at least 10 genes that contribute to variations in eye color , and at least 700 genes that contribute to differences in people’s height .","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h02","text":"Sex-Linked and Sex-Limited Genes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The genes on the sex chromosomes (designated X and Y in mammals) are known as sex-linked genes .","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"All other chromosomes are autosomal chromosomes, and their genes are known as autosomal genes .","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In mammals, a female has two X chromosomes, whereas a male has an X and a Y.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Psychological gender identification is another matter.) When biologists speak of sex-linked genes, they usually mean X-linked genes.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The small Y chromosome has a gene that causes the testes to form, but not as many genes as the X chromosome.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A man with the recessive form of this gene on his X chromosome is red-green color deficient because he has no other X chromosome.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Distinct from sex-linked genes are the sexlimited genes , present in both sexes but active mainly in one sex.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Both sexes have the genes, but sex hormones activate them in one sex and not the other, or one sex more than the other.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h03","text":"Genetic Changes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Changing a DNA base to any of the other three types means that the mutant gene will code for a protein with a different amino acid at one location in the molecule.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Given that evolution has already had eons to select the best makeup of each gene, most mutations are harmful, except when the environment changes.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, a mutation in a gene controlling the immune system might provide better protection against a new virus.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because some mutations occur as an embryo is developing or later, what we call “identical” twins can have genetic differences .","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because microduplications provide new material for genetic change, they have been a necessary part of our evolutionary history.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h04","text":"Epigenetics"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For psychology, the important aspect of epigenetics is that experiences can produce epigenetic changes, altering gene expression in the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Adding an acetyl group (COCH 3 ) to a histone tail loosens the histone’s grip on the DNA, facilitating the expression of the genes.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Removing an acetyl group tightens the histone’s grip on the DNA and silences the gene.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another epigenetic change is to add a methyl group (CH 3 ) at the beginning of a gene, turning it off, or removing a methyl group to turn it on .","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many experiences can alter the chemistry of the brain in a way that activates some genes and inactivates others.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exposing a pregnant mouse to alcohol changes the brain epigenetics of her offspring .","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If a mother rat is malnourished during pregnancy, her offspring alter the expression of certain genes to conserve energy and adjust to a world in which food will presumably be hard to find.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In humans, drug addiction produces epigenetic changes in the brain .","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Severe traumatic experiences in early childhood decrease methylation of many brain genes, increasing the later risk of depression or posttraumatic stress disorder .","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h05","text":"Heritability"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If the variation depends largely on genetic differences, the characteristic has high heritability .","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heritability ranges from zero, indicating no genetic contribution to the variation, to one, indicating complete control.","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people call monozygotic twins “identical,” a misleading term because the twins can differ, sometimes because of mutations that happened after conception.","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the biological mother contributes not only her genes but also the prenatal environment.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A heritability estimate shows how much something depends on variations in heredity within a population, and it varies from one population to another.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If some families have strict rules and others are lenient, the environmental influence is stronger, and therefore heritability will be lower.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although a heritability estimate is interesting, it is more useful to know which genes are important for an outcome, and how those genes exert their effects.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because that approach tests a huge number of hypotheses at once (one for each gene), it has a risk of seeing an apparent effect by accident.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To avoid an accidental finding, the researchers need to set an unusually high standard for statistical significance, and therefore they need to test tens or hundreds of thousands of people.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h06","text":"Environmental Modification"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A prime example is phenylketonuria (FEE-nil-KEET-uhn-YOOR-ee-uh), or PKU , a genetic inability to metabolize the amino acid phenylalanine.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If PKU is not treated, phenylalanine accumulates to toxic levels, impairing brain development and leaving a child cognitively impaired, restless, and irritable.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although PKU is a hereditary condition, environmental interventions can modify it.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physicians in many countries routinely test the level of phenylalanine or its metabolites in each baby’s blood.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If a baby has high levels, indicating PKU, physicians advise the parents to put the baby on a strict low-phenylalanine diet to protect the brain .","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People need to avoid meats, eggs, dairy products, grains, and especially aspartame (NutraSweet), which is 50 percent phenylalanine.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physicians formerly believed that children with PKU could quit the diet after a few years.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even a genetically normal baby cannot handle the enormous amounts of phenylalanine that an affected mother might pass through the placenta or milk.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h07","text":"How Genes Influence Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A gene can influence brain development, but it can influence behavior even without being expressed in the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If their reactions influence your personality, then your genes altered your behavior by altering your environment.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Now imagine a child born with genes promoting greater than average height and running speed.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of these factors, the child shows early success at basketball, and soon spends more and more time playing basketball.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a result, the child spends less time than average on other pursuits—watching videos, playing chess, or anything else.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The point is that genes can influence behavior in roundabout ways.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We should not be surprised that nearly every human behavior has some heritability.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h08","text":"The Evolution of Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evolution is a change over generations in the frequencies of various genes in a population.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, because humans are more similar to chimpanzees and bonobos than to other species, biologists infer a common ancestor.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As new evidence becomes available, biologists often change their opinions about the evolutionary relationship between one species and another.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, the question of how species do evolve is a question of how the process works, and that process is a necessary outcome from what we know about reproduction.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because plant and animal breeders have long understood this idea, they choose individuals with a desired trait and make them the parents of the next generation through a process called artificial selection .","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If certain individuals are more successful than others in finding food, escaping enemies, resisting illness, attracting mates, or protecting their offspring, then their genes will become more prevalent in later generations.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h09","text":"Misunderstandings about Evolution"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Let’s clarify the principles of evolution by addressing a few misconceptions:","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Natural selection cannot favor a gene that benefits the species while disadvantaging the individuals with the gene.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some people have claimed that when lemming populations become too high, some of the lemmings jump off cliffs to decrease the overpopulation problem.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If that were true (and it is not!), the next generation would all descend from lemmings that failed to jump.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h10","text":"Evolutionary Psychology"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It emphasizes evolutionary and functional explanations— that is, how our genes reflect those of our ancestors and why natural selection might have favored genes that promote certain behaviors.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The assumption is that any behavior characteristic of a species must have provided an advantage, at least in ancestral times.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, people get “goose bumps”—erections of the hairs, especially on their arms and shoulders—when they are cold or frightened.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Goose bumps produce little if any benefit to humans because our shoulder and arm hairs are short and usually covered by clothing.","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In most other mammals, however, erected hairs make a frightened animal look larger and more intimidating (Figure 4.6).","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Here is another example of an evolutionary explanation, this time relating to old age: Throughout the animal kingdom, and for plants as well, life does not outlast the capacity to reproduce.","sourcePrintedPage":112,"sourcePdfPage":130,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Living after you stop reproducing is disadvantageous from an evolutionary standpoint, because you would be competing with your offspring for food and shelter.","sourcePrintedPage":112,"sourcePdfPage":130,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Group selection works well for humans, because of our ability to punish or expel uncooperative people.","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"At its best, evolutionary psychology leads to research that helps us understand a behavior.","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The search for a functional explanation directs researchers to explore species’ different habitats and ways of life until we understand why they behave differently.","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The approach is criticized when its practitioners propose speculative explanations without supporting evidence .","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h11","text":"In Closing: Genes and Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many other behaviors are influenced by genes but also subject to strong influence by experience.","sourcePrintedPage":114,"sourcePdfPage":132,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Our genes and our evolution make it possible for humans to be what we are today, but they also give us the flexibility to change our behavior as circumstances warrant.","sourcePrintedPage":114,"sourcePdfPage":132,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Studying the genetics of behavior is more difficult with humans than with laboratory animals, because researchers have such limited control over environmental influences and no control over who mates with whom.","sourcePrintedPage":114,"sourcePdfPage":132,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Inferring how human behavior evolved is also difficult, because we do not know enough about the lives of our ancient ancestors.","sourcePrintedPage":114,"sourcePdfPage":132,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Certain genes influence the probability of developing Alzheimer’s disease or other conditions that occur mostly in old age.","sourcePrintedPage":115,"sourcePdfPage":133,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Prior to the work of Gregor Mendel in the late 19th century, scientists thought that inheritance was a blending process in which the properties of the sperm and the egg simply mixed, like two colors of paint.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":104,"sourcePdfPage":122},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, if three RNA bases are in the order cytosine, adenine, and guanine, then the protein adds the amino acid glutamine.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123},{"type":"bullet","text":"Any protein consists of some combination of 20 amino acids.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, you might have a gene for blue eyes on one chromosome and a gene for brown eyes on the other.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, a gene for brown eyes is dominant and a gene for blue eyes is recessive.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123},{"type":"bullet","text":"Each gene that contributes to eye color or height affects other characteristics as well.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124},{"type":"bullet","text":"Furthermore, changes in the environment can increase or decrease the expression of a gene.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124},{"type":"bullet","text":"So, for example, if 8 percent of human X chromosomes contain the gene for color vision deficiency, then 8 percent of men will be color deficient, but less than 1 percent of women will be (0.08 3 0.08).","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124},{"type":"bullet","text":"Examples include the genes that control the amount of chest hair in men, breast size in women, amount of crowing in roosters, and rate of egg production in hens.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124},{"type":"bullet","text":"A mutation is possible whenever a cell divides, not just at the time of conception.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125},{"type":"bullet","text":"During the process of reproduction, part of a chromosome that ordinarily appears once might instead appear twice or not at all.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125},{"type":"bullet","text":"The field of epigenetics deals with changes in gene expression.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125},{"type":"bullet","text":"The genes that are most active in your brain are not the same as those active in your lungs or kidneys, and those that are most active in one part of your brain may not be the most active in another part.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125},{"type":"bullet","text":"Many illustrations of the DNA molecule, as in Figure 4.2, show it as a straight line, which is an oversimplification.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125},{"type":"bullet","text":"In fact, proteins called histones bind DNA into a shape that is more like string wound around balls.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125},{"type":"bullet","text":"When male mice were exposed to chronic stressful experiences, their offspring showed a weakened hormonal response to stresses and altered gene expression in part of the brain.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126},{"type":"bullet","text":"The experience of feeling socially isolated or rejected alters the activity of hundreds of genes.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you sing better than someone else, the reason could be different genes, better training, or both.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers have relied mostly on studies of twins, supplemented by studies of adopted children.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126},{"type":"bullet","text":"Based on twin studies and adoption studies, researchers have found evidence for significant heritability of almost every behavior they have tested, including ability to postpone gratification, childhood misbehavior, cognitive performance, drawing style, educational success (J.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127},{"type":"bullet","text":"About the only behavior that has not shown a significant heritability is religious affiliation, such as Protestant or Catholic.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even a trait with high heritability can be modified by environmental interventions.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127},{"type":"bullet","text":"A woman with PKU should be especially careful during pregnancy and when nursing.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127},{"type":"bullet","text":"As a result, strangers smile at you and people want to get to know you.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128},{"type":"bullet","text":"Charles Darwin, known as the founder of evolutionary theory, didn’t like the term evolution.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128},{"type":"bullet","text":"He preferred descent with modification, emphasizing the idea of changes without necessarily implying improvement.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128},{"type":"bullet","text":"Given enough time, this process can produce the variety of life that we observe.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128},{"type":"bullet","text":"Note that the phrase “survival of the fittest” is misleading.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128},{"type":"bullet","text":"A “self-sacrificing” gene would die out with those who had it.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h09","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129},{"type":"bullet","text":"Several human behaviors make no sense except in terms of evolution.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":111,"sourcePdfPage":129},{"type":"bullet","text":"An infant will grasp tightly onto a finger or similar object in the palm of the hand.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":112,"sourcePdfPage":130},{"type":"bullet","text":"A mother monkey often needs all four limbs to search for food or to escape from a predator.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":112,"sourcePdfPage":130},{"type":"bullet","text":"(Grandfathers are sometimes useful too, but they are less dependable.) To further illustrate evolutionary psychology, consider the theoretically interesting example of altruistic behavior, an action that benefits someone other than the actor.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":112,"sourcePdfPage":130},{"type":"bullet","text":"Having other crows around means more eyes to watch for dangers.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":112,"sourcePdfPage":130},{"type":"bullet","text":"A gene spreads only if the individuals with it reproduce more than those without it.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131},{"type":"bullet","text":"A gene that fails to help the individual will not spread in the population.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you have genes that promote helpfulness toward your relatives, the behavior might generalize toward nonrelatives, especially if they resemble your relatives in some way.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another explanation is reciprocal altruism, the idea that individuals help those who will probably return the favor.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":113,"sourcePdfPage":131},{"type":"bullet","text":"In the control of behavior, genes are important but not all-important.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":114,"sourcePdfPage":132},{"type":"bullet","text":"Certain behaviors have a high heritability, such as the ability to taste PTC.","headingId":"bp14-m4-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":114,"sourcePdfPage":132}],"topicIds":["bp14-m4-1-h01","bp14-m4-1-h02","bp14-m4-1-h03","bp14-m4-1-h04","bp14-m4-1-h05","bp14-m4-1-h06","bp14-m4-1-h07","bp14-m4-1-h08","bp14-m4-1-h09","bp14-m4-1-h10","bp14-m4-1-h11"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m4-1-study-1","title":"Genes, environments, and development","text":"Genes influence biological systems through the production and regulation of proteins. Sex-linked genes reside on sex chromosomes, while sex-limited effects can depend on bodily context. .","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"If certain individuals are more successful than others in finding personality, then your genes altered your behavior by altering your environment.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"Now imagine a child born with genes promoting greater than average height and running speed.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"Because of these factors, the child shows early success at basketball, and soon spends more and more time playing basketball.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":69},{"text":"As a result, the child spends less time than average on other pursuits—watching videos, playing chess, or anything else.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"The point is that genes can influence behavior in roundabout ways.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"We heritability.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":72},{"text":"As a result, strangers smile at you and people want to .","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"If certain individuals are more successful than others in finding food, escaping enemies, resisting illness, attracting mates, or protecting their offspring, then their genes will become more prevalent in later generations.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"Charles Darwin, known as the founder of evolutionary with modification, emphasizing the idea of changes without necessarily implying improvement.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":128},{"text":"Given enough time, this process can produce the variety of life that we observe.","printedPage":110,"pdfPage":128,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":129},{"text":"Note that the phrase “survival of the fittest” is times.","printedPage":111,"pdfPage":129,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":87},{"text":"For example, people get “goose bumps”—erections of the hairs, especially on their arms and shoulders—when they are cold or frightened.","printedPage":111,"pdfPage":129,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":88},{"text":"Goose bumps produce little if any benefit to humans because our shoulder and arm hairs are short and usually covered by clothing.","printedPage":111,"pdfPage":129,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":89},{"text":"In most other mammals, however, erected hairs make a frightened animal look larger and more intimidating (Figure 4.6).","printedPage":111,"pdfPage":129,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":90},{"text":"Here reproduce.","printedPage":112,"pdfPage":130,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":91},{"text":"Living after you stop reproducing is disadvantageous from
